children: Global alternative asset management firm TPG-backed Newquest Asia Fund has offloaded a further Rs 200 crore worth of shares in Shadowfax Technologies, the technology-led third-party logistics company, through open market transactions on September 8.

As per the bulk deals data published by the BSE, Newquest Asia Fund IV (Singapore) sold 80 lakh shares, representing 1.36% of the paid-up equity, in Shadowfax. The shares were offloaded at Rs 250.03 apiece.

On the other side, Hong Kong-based investment firm Oxbow Capital Management-managed Oxbow Master Fund acquired an additional 47.85 lakh shares, equivalent to a 0.81% stake, for Rs 119.6 crore at Rs 250 per share.
This is the second transaction conducted by both investors in the September quarter.
With Tuesday's stake sale, Newquest has sold almost 3.5% stake in Shadowfax in the current quarter, reducing its shareholding to 8.03% from 11.53% as of June 2026.

However, Oxbow's name was not seen in the June quarter shareholding pattern. Hence, following the two transactions, Oxbow Master Fund's shareholding has increased to 2%, including the purchase of a 1.18% stake on August 6, 2026.
Shadowfax Technologies shares fell 0.18% to end at Rs 249.75 on Tuesday. Overall, the stock has been on an upward trajectory since February despite intermittent corrections and consolidation.
Four investors pick up 5.26% stake in Rays of Belief on listing day

Four investors together picked up a 5.26% stake in Rays of Belief, which operates under the MOM's Belief brand and provides personalised intervention and therapy plans for children with neurodevelopmental disorders.

Sachchiyay Stock Broking acquired 2.75 lakh shares for Rs 6.57 crore, Capacious Wealth Management LLP bought 2.25 lakh shares for Rs 5.37 crore, Santosh Bhansali HUF acquired 1.9 lakh shares for Rs 4.54 crore, and Pragya Mercantile bought 4.1 lakh shares for Rs 9.8 crore.
However, Longthrive Capital VCC - Trendview Capital Fund sold 1.43 lakh shares in Rays of Belief for Rs 3.42 crore. The buying and selling price was Rs 239 per share.
Rays of Belief shares corrected 4.46% to end at Rs 228.34 on the NSE on the first day of trading, against an issue price of Rs 239.
Vista Axis VCC-Quant Fund buys 0.5% stake in Sawaliya Food Products from Binaca
Vista Axis VCC-Quant Fund acquired 50,400 shares, representing 0.5% of the paid-up equity, in Sawaliya Food Products for Rs 85.68 lakh from Binaca. The shares changed hands at Rs 170 per share.
Binaca held a 1.42% stake in Sawaliya Food Products as of March 2026. Shares rebounded 6.28% to Rs 170 on the NSE on Tuesday after a recent sharp fall.
KJ Trust buys 0.58% stake in Texmaco Infra
KJ Trust acquired 7.39 lakh shares, equivalent to a 0.58% stake, in Texmaco Infrastructure & Holdings for Rs 8.86 crore at Rs 119.86 per share.
Texmaco Infrastructure shares ended at Rs 120.03, up 4.36%, extending their uptrend for the fourth consecutive session.

title: Shadowfax block deal: TPG-backed Newquest sells Rs 200 crore stake; Oxbow buys
